evals.prompt: I just cloned this plugin repo and want to get Claude talking to wp-devtools on it. Nothing's set up yet — no wp-env, no MCP client connected, I have no idea what WordPress version is even running.
evals.expected_output: The skill runs the Check (Preflight) step first: reports WordPress version, PHP version, Query Monitor/MCP Adapter availability, which local environment is in use, the enablement knob, and whether an MCP client is present — each gap paired with its exact fix. It does not install or enable anything during this step, and does not proceed to Install/enable until the developer has the picture and confirms.
expectations: The skill runs Check (Preflight) before anything else and does not skip straight to installing.
Every missing prerequisite is reported with the exact command or fix needed — not just flagged as missing.
No package manager command (composer, npm) is run during preflight — only inspected/reported.
The skill does not silently assume WordPress >= 6.9 or any other prerequisite — it checks and reports the actual finding.
The findings are presented together as one list, not drip-fed one at a time.

evals.prompt: This project was already scaffolded with the wp-tooling init engine (.wp-scaffold.json exists, npm run init is already in manage mode). Turn on the dev-tools feature and get me connected.
evals.expected_output: Preflight passes or reports only minor gaps. Install/enable invokes the init engine's dev-tools feature (npm run init -- --enable=dev-tools) rather than hand-wiring composer.json/.wp-env.json directly, and does not use --features= (which would clobber other already-enabled features). Connect runs or guides npm run dev:connect and confirms /mcp shows the server before calling the step done. Composer/npm installs are surfaced as developer actions, never run by the skill.
expectations: Because the init engine is present, the skill invokes the init engine's dev-tools feature via --enable=dev-tools rather than manually editing composer.json/.wp-env.json/package.json by hand, and does not use --features= for this.
The skill guides or runs npm run dev:connect for the Connect step.
The skill confirms /mcp shows the wp-dev-tools server connected before considering Connect complete.
No composer install/require or npm install is run by the skill itself — surfaced as a developer action only.
The skill proceeds through Check -> Install/enable -> Connect in that order, not out of sequence.

evals.prompt: This is an older plugin that doesn't have the wp-tooling init engine — no npm run init here. I still want dev-tools wired in by hand and connected.
evals.expected_output: Since the init engine isn't available, the skill guides the equivalent manual wiring: the composer.json repositories (VCS entry for rtCamp/wp-devtools) + require-dev entry for rtcamp/wp-dev-tools, then the same six settings (WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE, SAVEQUERIES, RT_DEV_TOOLS_DEV_MODE, RT_DEV_TOOLS_TELEMETRY_CONTAINER_ROOT/_HOST_ROOT/_LOOPBACK_BASE) plus the Query Monitor + MCP Adapter plugins — as a gitignored .wp-env.override.json (never the committed .wp-env.json) if the project uses wp-env, or as wp-config.php constants plus a manual plugin install otherwise. It also asks or infers which local environment is in use before picking the target, adds a .gitignore entry only when it wrote .wp-env.override.json, and wires the dev:connect/dev:disconnect scripts in package.json — each shown as a diff with consent requested before applying. No package manager command is run by the skill.
expectations: The skill detects or is told the init engine is unavailable and switches to guiding manual wiring rather than trying to invoke npm run init.
The skill does not assume wp-env — it asks or infers the local environment before deciding whether to target .wp-env.override.json or wp-config.php constants.
Each manual edit (composer.json, the local-env config, .gitignore where applicable, package.json) is shown as a diff with consent requested before being applied.

If the project uses wp-env, the wiring targets .wp-env.override.json (never the committed .wp-env.json) and the skill adds a .gitignore entry for it; on any other environment it targets wp-config.php constants instead, with no override file or .gitignore entry.
The config settings named are WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE, SAVEQUERIES, RT_DEV_TOOLS_DEV_MODE, and the RT_DEV_TOOLS_TELEMETRY_* keys — not a generic 'enablement knob' placeholder.
The composer wiring uses the correct hyphenation: rtcamp/wp-dev-tools as the require-dev package, https://github.com/rtCamp/wp-devtools.git as the VCS repository URL.
The skill does not run composer install, composer require, or npm install itself — these are surfaced as developer actions.
The skill still proceeds to Connect and Verify after the manual wiring is applied.

evals.prompt: wp-devtools is supposed to be connected already but /mcp doesn't show anything and Claude can't see any of its tools. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: The skill treats this as a Verify + Troubleshoot case rather than restarting from Check: it runs the verify smoke (abilities registered, tools/list, capture loop), identifies the likely cause from the troubleshoot table (dev:connect never run, MCP Adapter inactive, RT_DEV_TOOLS_DEV_MODE not true, wrong WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE), reports the diagnosis and the specific fix, and does not apply any file edit without consent.
expectations: The skill runs or references the Verify step's checks (abilities registered, tools/list, capture loop) to pin down what's actually broken rather than guessing.

The diagnosis maps the symptom to one of the documented likely causes (dev:connect not run, MCP Adapter inactive, RT_DEV_TOOLS_DEV_MODE not true, wrong WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE, wp-env not running) with its specific fix — not a vague 'enablement knob' placeholder.
The skill reports the diagnosis and fix rather than silently applying a change.
If a fix requires editing a file, the skill shows the diff and asks for consent before applying it.
The skill does not run any package manager command as part of troubleshooting.

evals.prompt: package.json has @rtcamp/wp-tooling and an init script, but nobody on the team has ever actually run npm run init — there's no .wp-scaffold.json. Can you turn on dev-tools?
evals.expected_output: The skill detects the init engine is present as a dependency but the project was never scaffolded (no .wp-scaffold.json), so npm run init would enter its first-run wizard rather than manage mode. It does not run npm run init -- --enable=dev-tools itself in this state, since that would drive the full first-run scaffold (project identity, capability selection) rather than just toggling a feature. It tells the developer to run npm run init themselves to complete that one-time setup, then offers to continue (toggle dev-tools via manage mode) once that's done.
expectations: The skill checks for .wp-scaffold.json and recognizes its absence means the project has never been scaffolded, not merely that dev-tools isn't enabled.
The skill does NOT invoke npm run init -- --enable=dev-tools (or any npm run init variant) itself in this state.
The skill explains that first run is a full scaffold wizard (project identity/capability choices) that only the developer should drive, and asks the developer to run npm run init themselves first.
The skill does not fall back to the fully-manual wiring path either (that's for projects with no init engine at all) — it correctly distinguishes 'engine present but never run' from 'no init engine'.
The skill offers to continue (enable dev-tools via manage mode) once the developer confirms npm run init has been completed.
